feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-heavy roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is slightly repetitive and could be tightened to improve impact and reduce overlap across skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within NACo strongly signal trust, growth, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Good use of scale and specificity: examples like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools/platforms add impact.  
- Strong executive profile: headline and summary clearly position you in digital strategy, platform modernization, and mission-driven communications.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and save space.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond activity: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more measurable business/organizational outcomes would strengthen impact.  
- Minor style/grammar consistency issues: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); consider consistent capitalization/style for terms like “front-end,” “organization-wide,” and date abbreviations (“Sept.”/“Oct.”). No major misspellings or typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s direction, but it reads a bit generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with sharper positioning tied to recent leadership in digital transformation, Drupal/web modernization, and analytics-enabled communications.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and fix style: use “12+ years of experience” instead of “more than 12 years experience.”
- Lead with current marketable positioning: digital strategy, web modernization, and cross-channel leadership for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Add 1–2 concrete differentiators from recent roles, such as enterprise website migration, analytics/governance, or building scalable editorial systems.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social media, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Specializes in cross-channel strategy, Drupal/web modernization, analytics, and editorial systems that improve governance, usability, and team coordination. Brings deep experience in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating complex policy or technical topics into clear, audience-focused content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “stakeholder coordination” are already echoed in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- Avoid overloading the intro with multimedia or workflow language if those are already detailed in experience bullets.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant mix of strategic, technical, and operational strengths, but several items are broad and overlap heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening wording and making competencies more distinctive will improve scan value.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, CV-specific terms: “Multi-channel communications leadership,” “CMS modernization & administration,” “Editorial systems & governance,” “Analytics, KPI reporting & optimization.”
- Reduce overlap by combining similar items: merge “Editorial workflow design” with “Workflow & systems architecture,” and shorten “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” to “Cross-functional stakeholder coordination.”
- Use parallel noun phrases and consistent style throughout; “communication” should be plural for consistency.
- Possible rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • CMS administration & web operations • Editorial systems, governance & workflow design • Analytics, KPI reporting & optimization • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital strategy & transformation” and “Policy & advocacy communications” repeat themes already stated in the header.
- Several items closely mirror Topline Skills, especially editorial systems, multi-channel communications, and analytics.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Tighten it around scope, platform leadership, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or flagship initiatives.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary line: “Embedded as a full-time strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvement, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Combine overlapping bullets and lead with impact: “Built and optimized digital systems, workflows, and analytics to improve coordination across enterprise communications.”
- Make Drupal/web work more outcome-focused: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- Tighten the technical/AI bullets: “Delivered front-end/CMS enhancements for high-traffic public web properties and led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content, and user discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI search and microsite examples already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and save specifics for the project section.
- Governance/analytics language overlaps with prior NACo roles and the summary; avoid repeating the same phrasing.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a national membership organization.”
- Combine the strongest achievements into outcome-led bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more explicit where possible: add budget/team size, % efficiency gains, reporting adoption, production cost savings, or engagement growth from the studio and analytics work.
- Tighten weaker phrasing: replace “Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels...” with specifics on volume, growth, engagement, or campaign results.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Email/social/video channel management overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; emphasize enterprise leadership, platform modernization, and governance here.
- Video production also appears in older NACo roles; keep this version focused on building the in-house studio as a strategic capacity upgrade.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more specific to operational ownership, editorial systems, and channel growth during this period.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing across multiple internal teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Add outcome language where possible: “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel” and include views, open rates, or production cadence if available.
- Rephrase vague bullets with concrete systems impact: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes connecting communications, advocacy and program staff” and “Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency and speed.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “video as a recurring channel” overlaps with the footer project and 2015–2018 role; distinguish this role as scaling/formalizing it.
- Avoid repeating broad channel oversight already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 Director entry.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent roles. It should be tighter and more distinctive, emphasizing leadership scope rather than repeating generic communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less redundant phrasing:  
- Enterprise digital strategy  
- Editorial governance and content operations  
- Cross-channel communications leadership  
- Public-sector digital engagement  
- Audience and journey-based content planning
- Consider swapping “public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “mission-driven stakeholder communications” if targeting broader roles beyond advocacy.
- Keep terms parallel and noun-based; avoid mixing strategy, messaging, and planning language inconsistently.
- If space allows, prioritize “content operations” over “messaging,” since it better reflects recent senior work and differentiates from older communications-heavy roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with both Core Competencies and multiple NACo experience bullets.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

- SharePoint

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and group tools more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences**
- Remove lower-priority or older items here: cut **jQuery** and consider dropping **WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages** from Topline Skills unless central to target roles.
- Lead with the most marketable and recent strengths tied to current work: **Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations, automation**.
- If possible, align wording to outcomes shown elsewhere, e.g. “enterprise CMS modernization” and “search/discovery experiences” to reinforce the 10,000+ page migration and AI search project.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the detailed platform/tool inventory already covered in **Technical + IT**.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlaps with **Core Competencies**; keep phrasing distinct or shorten here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory rather than a senior-level capability statement. It should emphasize decision support and optimization outcomes, while avoiding overlap with the “Technical + IT” analytics list.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization” rather than just product names.
- Tighten and group items by function: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” then “KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive dashboarding and decision support” for stronger seniority.
- Optional rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • Executive dashboarding and decision support • SEO and digital performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills more strategic and save full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value production leadership and event delivery rather than listing generic tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task-level skills to capability-level strengths: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “Livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “Studio and PTZ camera operations.”

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent CMS expertise or expanded with level/context.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize by depth and recency: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites)** • **WordPress** • **SharePoint** • **Power Pages** • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, add proficiency cues instead of just names: **Drupal (advanced)** • **WordPress (advanced)** • SharePoint (working) • Power Pages (working) • GitHub Pages
- Consider renaming to **CMS & Web Platform Administration** to sound more senior and operational.
- If you want stronger impact, replace GitHub Pages with a more relevant platform/tool unless it reflects meaningful recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep this version shorter and more platform-specific.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid repeating generic CMS claims elsewhere.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list rather than a differentiated skills item. It should better reflect current, relevant implementation strengths and align with the senior platform/automation focus in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw languages to applied capability areas: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Drop version numbers unless used elsewhere consistently; “HTML” and “CSS” are cleaner than “HTML5/CSS3.”
- Put the strongest, more current tools first; if Cloudflare Workers and GitHub Actions are recent hands-on tools, move them ahead of jQuery.
- If accurate, add scope or outcome in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., automation, deployment, or performance improvements enabled by these tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; consider trimming one section or making this version more implementation-specific.
- GTM may overlap with analytics infrastructure; keep it here only if you actively implemented tagging, not just managed analytics.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design capability. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more clearly differentiated.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Group by function to improve scanability: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/Workflow Management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show depth: **Built and managed workflow systems in Airtable, Power Automate and Zapier; coordinated delivery through Jira, Asana and Trello**
- Drop weaker/older tools if space is tight; keep the platforms most aligned to recent consulting and digital operations work

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; include only if they support a broader workflow/operations story

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, especially given your recent leadership over email/newsletter operations, but it’s currently just a vendor list. It would be stronger if framed around capability and aligned to the platforms most clearly supported by your experience.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp (campaign operations, newsletter publishing, audience segmentation)**
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work: **email campaign delivery, member communications, and engagement workflows**
- Keep it concise; this section should show tool familiarity, not repeat achievements already covered in NACo roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding metrics here like “tens of thousands of subscribers”; that’s already stronger in Work Experience.
- “Engagement” overlaps with broader communications claims elsewhere, so anchor this item specifically to **email/member platform systems**.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content operations, and any concrete outputs.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: website size/traffic at the time, number of livestreams/videos produced, cadence of weekly updates, or team size supported.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; replace with specifics such as “supported website refresh,” “produced weekly advocacy videos,” and “supervised one digital media associate.”
- Possible version: “Promoted across two roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, standardizing workflows across web, email, social, and video. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day supervision to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching/building the format rather than expanding it.
- Avoid repeating website/governance language already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 entry.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in multimedia. Keep it brief, emphasize the “first podcast” as the clearest differentiator, and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities.”
- Add a second sentence focused on the standout media contribution: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a more specific verb, e.g., “produced” or “supported production of digital and multimedia content.”
- If possible, add scope: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders, or types of projects supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid broad multimedia language that repeats later video/content leadership entries.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here; later NACo roles already show progression into team and platform ownership.
